# Zeroshot

> Zeroshot enforces your team's QA process on coding agents. You define the process as a graph: which agents implement, which independent agents review or test the result, where rejected work goes for repair, and where a run stops. The engine runs the graph's order, routing and bounds in code, so no agent can skip a step; model output cannot add an edge or raise a bound. It is a native CLI (`zeroshot`) for Linux, macOS, and Windows, driving Codex, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, or Pi, and each node can use its own harness and model. MIT licensed.

## Why teams use it

- One process for the whole team. The standards live in one graph, saved as a profile, that every engineer's tasks run through, instead of in each person's prompts and skills.
- Independent review. In the built-in graph, separate acceptance and code-review agents decide whether the work passes, and rejected work goes to repair until both accept or the run's bounds are reached.
- You choose where a run stops: a local change, a pushed branch, a reviewed pull request, or a merge after CI.
- It is built for teams whose agents write code faster than anyone can review it.

## Make it yours

- Start from the built-in `software-change` graph (implementation, then acceptance and code review in parallel, then bounded repair) and add the stages your team requires: adversarial bug-finding, end-to-end tests, or security review and a blast-radius map for changes to auth, payments, or migrations.
- `zeroshot template show software-change --delivery none` prints the built-in graph as an editable `GraphSpec`; run your version with `--graph my-graph.json`.
- Choose each node's harness, model, effort, and instructions, which steps run in parallel, and where failures route. Codex can implement while Claude Code reviews.
- Save the graph with its runtime settings as a profile (`--profile`), locally or for your organization on Zeroshot Cloud, so everyone runs the same process. The browser UI (`zeroshot ui`) edits profiles and shows runs.

## Also included

- Delivery: `software-change` opens a pull request by default and addresses visible review feedback and required CI without merging. That needs a committed Git checkout with an HTTPS or SSH remote and, for GitHub, the `gh` CLI. `--delivery none` keeps the change local, `--push` pushes the run branch without a pull request, and `--ship` follows the repository's merge policy through to a merged revision.
- Execution targets: local, a self-hosted Docker target, or Zeroshot Cloud (shared team queue, durable run history). Failed runs with a recoverable workspace can resume from a checkpoint.
- Every run records its events in a durable SQLite ledger.
- An `auto-research` graph runs ten bounded experiment iterations with independent review of evidence, method, and progress.
- Experimental: expose a graph as an ACP agent with `zeroshot acp`.

## When to use it

- Your team wants one QA process that every agent-written change goes through.
- A change should be checked by agents other than the one that wrote it.
- You want the result delivered as a branch, a reviewed pull request, or a merge after CI.
- You want the same review and repair setup reused across tasks, locally, self-hosted, or in the cloud.

## When not to use it

- A small edit you will review yourself in the editor; a single agent session is quicker.
- As a replacement for tests. A passing run means the configured checks accepted the work; coverage depends on the requirements, reviewers, and tests you provide.
- Per-edit checking inside an agent session: that is Opcore (https://github.com/the-open-engine/opcore), which pairs with Zeroshot.

## Install and first run

```bash
npm install -g @the-open-engine-company/zeroshot
echo '{"task": "Add JSON output to the status command and cover it with focused tests."}' > input.json
echo '{"harness": "codex", "provider": "openai", "model": "YOUR_MODEL_ID", "effort": "high"}' > runtime.json
zeroshot run --title "Add JSON status output" --template software-change --delivery none \
  --input input.json --uniform-runtime-config runtime.json --validate-only
```

Replace `YOUR_MODEL_ID` with a model your installed Codex CLI supports. A valid request prints `{"valid":true}`; drop `--validate-only` to start the run. The worker edits the selected folder (`--cwd FOLDER`). `--delivery none` keeps the change local, so Git is optional; without it the run opens a pull request.

For another harness, change `harness` and `provider` in `runtime.json`: `claude` with `anthropic` for Claude Code, `copilot` with `github` for GitHub Copilot, or `pi` with `anthropic` or `openai`. The [first-run guide](https://zeroshot.sh/docs/current/getting-started/first-run/) has each file. Model identifiers pass to the harness unchanged; Zeroshot keeps no model catalog.

The installer needs Node.js 18+ and installs a verified native binary plus the `zeroshot` and `zeroshot-memory-init` skills for Codex, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, and Pi. Local runs reuse the harness's existing login, so no API key is needed. The [install guide](https://zeroshot.sh/docs/current/getting-started/install/) says where the skills go and how to remove them.

The CLI is free and open source (MIT). Model calls go through your own harness login or provider account.

- [Install](https://zeroshot.sh/docs/current/getting-started/install/): prerequisites and harness setup
- [First run](https://zeroshot.sh/docs/current/getting-started/first-run/): input, runtime config, and inspecting a run
- [Execution](https://zeroshot.sh/docs/current/concepts/execution/): built-in graphs and delivery behavior
- [Runtimes and connections](https://zeroshot.sh/docs/current/concepts/runtimes-and-connections/): supported harness and provider pairs
- [Graph contract](https://zeroshot.sh/docs/current/reference/cluster/graph/): authoring custom graphs
- [Build a review loop](https://zeroshot.sh/docs/current/guides/review-loop/): a worked custom graph and runtime plan
- [RuntimePlan reference](https://zeroshot.sh/docs/current/reference/runtime-plan/): every runtime binding field and admission limit
- [Observe and control runs](https://zeroshot.sh/docs/current/guides/observe-and-control/): status, logs, resume
- [CLI reference](https://zeroshot.sh/docs/current/zeroshot-cli/)
- [Zeroshot Cloud docs](https://cloud.zeroshot.sh/docs): organizations, GitHub App, connections, profiles, and issue-triggered runs
